newsitem.title: UK: Market regulators invited to London meeting.
newsitem.headline: Market regulators invited to London meeting.

text.p: Regulators from up to 18 countries will attend a November 25/26 meeting in London covering futures markets in deliverable commodities.

The two-day meeting -- co-hosted by Britain's senior financial regulator the Securities and Investment Board (SIB), the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and Japan's Ministries of International Trade and Investment (MITI) and Agriculture and Fisheries (MAF) -- have invited regulators from 15 other countries to attend.

David Pritchard, head of SIB's markets and exchanges division who is heading SIB's review of global metal markets, said the timing of the meeting will give regulators an opportunity to benefit from the responses to the questionaire SIB sent out as part of its review of the world's metal markets.
This review is due to be completed before Christmas.
The meeting will cover all types of physical commodities exchanges including those based on a reference price and cash settled like the International Petroleum Exchange's crude oil contract.
